henry.title: How NNR and Henry calculate energy

rest.title: Energy at rest
rest.description: NNR 2023 uses the Henry equations (Oxford, 2005) for resting energy. The app uses your weight, height and biological sex with the NNR age bands 18–24, 25–50 and 51+ years.

formula.title: Weight and height in the equation

activity.title: Daily needs with PAL
activity.description: Resting energy is multiplied by the selected PAL activity factor and by 239 to convert MJ to kcal. PAL 1.4, 1.6 and 1.8 are the NNR reference levels for low, moderate and high activity.

estimate.title: An estimate
estimate.description: The result estimates maintenance needs. The app uses your own measurements rather than the reference measurements in the NNR tables. The app has no automatic estimate for intersex people; set a goal manually instead.

proteinReference.title: Protein according to WHO and NNR
proteinReference.description: NNR 2023 gives 15% of energy from protein as a planning target for adults and 18% for older adults, with a recommended range of 1.2–1.5 g/kg per day for older adults. The app uses 18% and at least 1.5 g/kg from age 65. Below age 65, it uses 15% and at least 0.83 g/kg, in line with NNR and the WHO/FAO/UNU reference for healthy adults. The weight-based minimum takes priority and may result in a higher protein share than the preset percentage. Enter your weight and birth date to personalise the target.

energyProductionCharts.title: Energy metrics
energyProductionCharts.explainer: VO₂ max, resting heart rate, and HRV are three key indicators of your fitness and energy production capacity. Tap a metric to view its trend.

explainers.vo2_max: VO₂ max indicates mitochondrial density and oxidative capacity. Higher values = more efficient ATP production from oxygen.
explainers.resting_hr: Resting heart rate reflects baseline cardiovascular load and recovery state. A lower resting heart rate is often associated with better fitness and energy efficiency.
explainers.hrv: HRV reflects autonomic nervous system balance and recovery readiness. Higher HRV is often a sign of better stress resilience and energy regulation.

sleepTrendChart.title: Sleep trends
sleepTrendChart.explainer: Tap different metrics to view their trends over time.

explainers.sleep_duration: Sleep duration shows your total nightly recovery. A stable level around 7 to 9 hours supports hormone balance, immune function, and mental sharpness.
explainers.deep_sleep: Deep sleep is the phase where the body prioritizes physical recovery, tissue repair, and immune support. The trend helps show whether recovery is actually improving over time.
explainers.rem_sleep: REM sleep supports memory consolidation, emotional processing, and learning. Tracking REM over time gives a better signal of stress, sleep quality, and mental recovery.
explainers.sleep_bedtime: Bedtime consistency is one of the most powerful levers for sleep quality. The trend shows whether your sleep timing is becoming more stable — a key factor for circadian rhythm and overall recovery.
explainers.intense_exercise_before_sleep: Intense exercise before sleep can negatively impact sleep quality. The trend shows whether evening workouts affect your recovery over time.

todaysActivityCharts.title: Today's activity
todaysActivityCharts.explainer: Regular movement throughout the day maintains mitochondrial health. Even light activity (walking) stimulates ATP production and reduces oxidative stress.

explainers.activity_minutes: Total minutes of activity today. Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate or 75 minutes of vigorous activity per week to support mitochondrial function.
explainers.steps: Your total steps for the day. Aim for consistent movement to support energy levels and metabolic health.
explainers.intensity_minutes: Minutes of elevated heart rate. Both moderate and vigorous activity boost mitochondrial function and overall fitness.

digestiveTrendsChart.title: Digestive Health Drivers
digestiveTrendsChart.explainer: HRV, sleep, and activity all influence digestion, gut barrier function, and microbiome balance. Tap a metric to see how its trend changes over time.

explainers.hrv: HRV reflects stress load and recovery through autonomic balance. Prolonged stress can negatively affect gut barrier function, motility, and microbiome stability.
explainers.sleep_duration: Sufficient and consistent sleep supports gut recovery, hormone balance, and microbiome circadian rhythm. Short or irregular sleep can worsen digestion over time.
explainers.active_minutes: Regular movement supports gut motility, circulation, and metabolic health. Over time, this can improve digestive function and reduce gastrointestinal discomfort.

mindTrendsChart.title: Cognitive metrics
mindTrendsChart.explainer: Tap different metrics to view their trends over time.

explainers.sleep_duration: Sleep duration in hours and minutes shows your recovery baseline. A stable level night after night supports memory, concentration, and emotional regulation.
explainers.steps: The steps trend reflects your daily movement volume. Consistent everyday activity supports brain blood flow and can improve cognitive sharpness.
explainers.intensity_minutes: Intensity minutes show how much pulse-raising activity you get. The right weekly dose can improve stress resilience and mental performance.

immuneTrendsChart.title: Immune status
immuneTrendsChart.explainer: Your immune resilience is shaped by recovery, stress regulation, and physiological load. Tap a metric to view its trend over time and spot early signs of imbalance.

explainers.sleep_duration: Adequate sleep duration supports immune signaling and lowers inflammatory load. The trend helps you see whether your recovery foundation is stable week to week.
explainers.deep_sleep: Deep sleep is the most immune-supportive sleep stage, where tissue repair and immune regulation are prioritized. A declining trend can indicate growing vulnerability.
explainers.resting_hr: Resting heart rate is a sensitive load marker. An unusual upward trend can be an early signal of infection, inflammation, or under-recovery.
explainers.hrv: HRV reflects autonomic balance and recovery capacity. Higher, more stable levels are often associated with stronger immune response and stress resilience.
explainers.recovery: Recovery status is estimated from HRV (45%), resting heart rate (30%), and sleep (25%), compared with your baseline over the previous 28 days.

nervousTrendsChart.title: Nervous system trends
nervousTrendsChart.explainer: Tap HRV or resting heart rate to see their trends over time.

explainers.hrv: The HRV trend shows how effectively your autonomic system shifts into recovery. Higher and steadier levels often indicate better stress resilience.
explainers.resting_hr: Resting heart rate is a sensitive stress and recovery marker. A gradual upward trend can be an early sign of under-recovery.
explainers.recovery: Recovery status is estimated from HRV (45%), resting heart rate (30%), and sleep (25%), compared with your baseline over the previous 28 days.

cardioTrendsChart.explainer: Tap VO₂ max, resting heart rate, or training load to view their trends over time.

explainers.vo2_max: The VO₂ max trend shows how your peak oxygen uptake develops over time. It's the gold standard for cardiovascular fitness — a rising curve is a clear sign of improvement.
explainers.resting_hr: Resting heart rate reflects cardiac efficiency at rest. A declining trend over time is a positive sign of improved cardiovascular fitness and lower stress load.
explainers.training_load: Training load shows weekly volume of activity and intensity minutes. The reference lines at 150 and 300 help you keep load in the right zone.
